Use-case & requirements summary:
- Workload: near-real-time support-agent suggestions + doc-search fallback for knowledge-base answers. High throughput during spikes (50-150 reqs/min) but generally bursty.
- Targets: 95th pct API latency < 400ms for short completions, connection establishment <100ms where possible.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate (SMB), wants predictable per-response costs and ability to route cheaper models for background tasks.
- Model preferences: open to gpt-style open models; wants Redwood to recommend quantized / smaller variants for background rerankings.
- Routing/fallback needs: region affinity (EU) and model-tier fallback for capacity/concurrency.
- Security: SOC2 posture important; audit logs for agent prompts desirable but not blocking.

SE notes / quick perf tuning advice given to customer (copied in CRM):
- Region selection: confirm SDK/endpoint explicitly set to eu-west-1 for EU traffic. Some early tests were hitting us-west — missed env var.
- Connection reuse: use persistent HTTP/2 connections for streaming; avoid new TLS handshake per request.
- Client timeouts: set client-side read timeout to 30s but use shorter application-level abort for UI interactions (8-12s) so agent UI can degrade gracefully.
- Streaming vs blocking: switch to streaming responses for agent suggestions — start rendering tokens at ~150ms after first token, reduces perceived latency.
- Prompt engineering: reduce context size — send only active conversation + most relevant KB snippet (use retrieval with 2-3 chunks), avoid sending full ticket history each request. Compress system instructions and normalize templates.
- Batching & concurrency: for high burstiness, implement small (2-4) concurrent inflight requests with token limits instead of large batch delays.
- Fallbacks: configure routing policy to use smaller/cheaper model (e.g., L0 quantized variant) for non-interactive reranking or background summarization.
- Warm cache: for frequent KB queries, enable prefix/KV cache and pre-warm endpoints during peak hours.
- Metrics to capture: client-side rtt, server token latency, model selection, connection reuse stats.
